Security note: the blocklist-subscription fetcher (crates/lodestar/src/subscriptions.rs) used a plain HTTP client that bypassed the §16 SSRF guard (private/metadata hosts, redirect hops). No API could add a subscription before, so it wasn't reachable; #362 (B-subscriptions-api) adds the subscribe route, and the runner required routing fetches through the guard before merge. Also: a password-gated "accept narrowed version" is now bound to both the applied and held versions.

Owner question (privacy trade-off, from #362): blocklist list fetches now go through the SSRF guard, which by §16 ignores system proxies (HTTPS_PROXY), because a proxy resolves names itself and would bypass the private-address check. §20.13 had said list fetches use the proxy egress. Effect: a user who relies on HTTPS_PROXY (not a whole-container VPN such as gluetun, which still applies) would fetch blocklists from their own IP. Lists on the local network, including config lists, are now refused. Recommendation: accept for v0.6 (gluetun is the documented setup); a follow-up could add a guarded proxy mode. main is not shipped, so this can be changed before the v0.6 cut.

Owner question (content safety, from #367 F-filter-standin-undo): when an unreadable "Is adult" classification rule becomes readable again, the adult holds its stand-in made are NOT released automatically, because storage can't tell them apart from a user's own per-torrent adult correction (releasing could undo a user's child-safety choice permanently). Automatic release would need a change to the stored rule-id format recording what made a hold adult (e.g. "CS-5a~C-2+adult"), plus writer and reclassify changes.
